status: Accepted ordinary RH proof for the actual all-length averaged statistic.
scope: Entire frozen proof read, primary CCCC inputs checked in this and prior reviewed turns, Schoenfeld Theorem10/(6.2) read from cached primary text and publisher-indexed page. No symbolic checker replay or novelty claim.
verified: Actual prime interval multiplier exp(lambda/T), exact center (exp(lambda/T)-1)x, all Lambda prime powers and fixed x in [T^(7/4),T^(9/4)] are retained.
Exact S=1/(exp(lambda/T)-1), r=log S/log T reparameterization gives V_(lambda,T)=(T/S)r² V_lin_(1,S)(omega(r dot)).
For lambda<=sqrt(T), one fixed Selberg window exponent B=3b+3 contains the original support. Known RH bound yields lambda(1+|log lambda|)^2 near zero and O(lambda) above one, uniformly.

For lambda>sqrt(T), exact centering permits E(exp(lambda/T)x)-E(x). The RH Chebyshev bound yields (T/log T)exp(lambda/T)(log T+lambda/T+1)^4; exp(-lambda) makes the all-length statistic finite for T>=2 and this tail o(1).

On fixed compact lambda ranges, varying weights can be replaced by one fixed smooth-square test using a positive Selberg mass bound before using CCCC. This supplies genuine uniformity without assuming uniform Schwartz seminorm errors.
Smoothed zero measures depend on lambda via S; only their integrated mass is replaced by 2y C_(Ty) on compact y ranges using the source's uniform logarithmic range.

Both y tails checked. After the height limit at fixed length range, constants for intermediate-range tails come from a common fixed-test spectral mass bound; the integrated lower tail is O(eta), upper tail O(1/R).
Finite-range integration by parts differentiates only the explicit kernel. Averaging and removing auxiliary cutoffs yields k=1/[2(1+y²)] and probability density p=4y²/[pi(1+y²)²].
The common compact mass bound justifies the smooth-square approximation with T limit before approximation limit.
Vbar=integral p(y)C_(Ty)dy+o(1), limsup Vbar<=A, and A-Vbar=integral p(y)D_(Ty)dy+o(1) follow for the exact R16 bump. These statements do not require AH.

Combining with the independently reviewed height-regularity proof at SHA6048b879 gives 2d²/(25pi A)<=A-liminf Vbar<=d, d=limsup D. The previously conditional dependency is discharged within these two ordinary proofs.
limitations: This is a different length-averaged statistic, not an improved bound for R19's fixed single length.
The upper bound equals the AH saturation value; no strict arithmetic deficit is proved.
No finite-height error rate, optimality, novelty, formal verification, actual RH proof or AH refutation.
